law.sustainable_deployment_ceiling: Y<=b*N; if b=1 the non-drifting boundary is Y=N

synthetic_implications: With recurring constant intake and positive training rate, faster training changes transient lag and trainee inventory but not long-run graduation throughput.
The long-run trained output ceiling is set by recurring intake; reserve attrition then reduces sustainable deployable throughput from N to b*N per interval.
A force-generation system can therefore be training-lag limited in the short run but intake/attrition limited in the long run.
Increasing training speed alone cannot raise the asymptotic throughput above recurring intake once the pipeline has equilibrated.
claim_boundary: SL12 is an exact recurrence theorem of Pineland's synthetic security training/reserve mechanism, not an empirical force-generation throughput law.
